[41].course_content_by_year[2].modules[8].title: Entrepreneurship and Innovation
[41].course_content_by_year[2].modules[8].description: This module aims to equip students with an applied understanding of entrepreneurs and their activities in a wide range of contemporary settings.
[41].course_content_by_year[2].modules[9].title: Decision and Efficiency Analysis
[41].course_content_by_year[2].modules[9].description: The aims of the module are to: develop an understanding of the complex multidimensional nature of decision and efficiency analysis problems faced by managers and policy makers; develop skills in modelling decision and efficiency analysis problems; obtain hands-on experience with the use of computers for decision and efficiency analysis in a business or policy environment; demonstrate the usefulness of decision and efficiency analysis in a global economic context; examine the societal and ethical implications of decision and efficiency analysis.
[41].course_content_by_year[2].modules[10].title: Corporate Governance
[41].course_content_by_year[2].modules[10].description: The aims of this module are: To provide an introduction to corporate governance in the UK; To provide an understanding of different governance mechanisms; To develop relevant transferable skills
[41].course_content_by_year[2].modules[11].title: Business Systems
[41].course_content_by_year[2].modules[11].description: The aims of this module are: to develop an appreciation of the use of Management Information Systems in business contexts, particularly in management planning, decision-making and control; to develop a critical perspective on Information Systems within contemporary organisations and society; to build on previous modules which introduced management aspects of Information Systems and on students' experience of working with such systems during the Industrial & Professional Studies year.
[41].course_content_by_year[2].modules[12].title: University-wide Language Programme
[41].course_content_by_year[2].modules[12].description: This is a 10 credit module from the University-wide language programme.
[41].course_content_by_year[2].modules[13].title: Corporate Finance and Derivatives
[41].course_content_by_year[2].modules[13].description: The aims of this module are to provide: a sound practical and theoretical understanding of corporate finance, in particular corporate investment decisions awareness of the major derivative products and markets conceptual understanding of arbitrage pricing of financial derivatives practical experience of implementing some of the most widely used corporate finance and derivative pricing models.
[41].course_content_by_year[2].modules[14].title: Research and Communication Skills for Economists
[41].course_content_by_year[2].modules[14].description: The aim of this module is to equip students with core skills which are valued highly by employers. Students will learn how to think and research like economists when evaluating policy and business related problems. They will also develop the skills to communicate and present their analysis confidently and persuasively. The emphasis throughout is on gaining skills and attitudes that support the application of economics to questions of contemporary relevance.
[41].course_content_by_year[2].modules[15].title: Multinational Financial Management
[41].course_content_by_year[2].modules[15].description: The aims of this module are to: build on the pre-requisite modules develop an understanding of the practice of financial management in companies operating in the international environment develop an understanding of balance of payment dynamics, international capital flows and nature of currency attacks develop critical reasoning skills in the context of international financial risk management. This course explores managing international business and global competition with an understanding of international financial instruments, markets and institutions.
[41].course_content_by_year[2].modules[16].title: Business Optimisation
[41].course_content_by_year[2].modules[16].description: The aims of this module are to: develop the ability to build models to help managers optimise a range of business processes and decisions; further develop the concepts and skills required to a software use to help managers in decision making.
[41].course_content_by_year[2].modules[17].title: Industrial Economics
[41].course_content_by_year[2].modules[17].description: The aim of the module is to develop economic skills to analyse strategic interaction among firms in imperfectly competitive markets or regulated industries.
[41].course_content_by_year[2].modules[18].title: Central Banking and Financial Crises
[41].course_content_by_year[2].modules[18].description: The aim of this module is for the student to appreciate how and why central banks use monetary policy, with a view to understanding noteworthy recent and historical policy developments in the UK, the US, Japan, and the Euro area. Part of the module is geared towards understanding how central banks react to financial crises, with special emphasis placed on the recent global financial crisis, as well as important historical events such as the great depression. The module aims to make students appreciate how the central bank is at the heart of a country's financial and economic system.
[41].course_content_by_year[2].modules[19].title: Managerial Economics
[41].course_content_by_year[2].modules[19].description: The module aims to link economic theory to management disciplines. Students will explore the ways in which managers can exploit economic theories to inform their decision-making processes and the impact it has at the macro level. Students will study the economics of management and organisation practices at the firm level. Students will also examine problems faced by managers and will gain a better understanding of the external environment in which the organisation operates. The module will also emphasise the role of corporate governance in the broader corporate environment.
[41].course_content_by_year[2].modules[20].title: Labour Economics
[41].course_content_by_year[2].modules[20].description: The module aims to introduce students to key theories in the analysis of labour markets and to develop both a knowledge of empirical evidence and the capacity to evaluate critically the evidence available. The module will introduce students to recent developments in labour economics research and at the same time discuss policy relevant topics.
[41].course_content_by_year[2].modules[21].title: Development Economics
[41].course_content_by_year[2].modules[21].description: This module aims to introduce students to development economics, which is the study of how economies are transformed to overcome problems of absolute poverty, from low-income to high-income status and also from stagnation to growth. The main focus of this module is on the world's poorest. The module examines essential aspects of the economic lives of the poor including poverty and income inequality; gender inequality; human capital - health and education; population growth; financial aid and access; and civil and ethnic conflicts. In part, this module also aims to examine how markets and institutions work (or do not work) for the poor as a basis for understanding development policy debates.
[41].course_content_by_year[2].modules[22].title: Behavioural Finance
[41].course_content_by_year[2].modules[22].description: The aims of this module are to: provide an understanding of mathematical models of behavioural foundations of financial decisions; develop skills that will enable students to critically analyse financial decisions in greater depth; deepen and broaden students' conceptual understanding of how financial markets 'actually work' and how people 'actually make decisions' using real-life cases and experimental results.
[41].course_content_by_year[2].modules[23].title: Rethinking Leadership: Theory and Practice
[41].course_content_by_year[2].modules[23].description: The aim of this module is to examine the roles of leadership in contributing to organisational and individual outcomes, as well as preparing students for their development into leadership roles.
[41].course_content_by_year[2].modules[24].title: Project Management

[5].course_overview: Business with a Foundation Year for Elite Athletes enables entry into any of our Business courses for students that are classed as elite athletes by our performance sport centre and have not got the qualifications required for direct entry.

Our Foundation Studies programme at Loughborough is designed to help a range of students realise their university ambitions. Our streamed approach enables you to progress on to one of multiple courses within your chosen stream – giving you further time to decide which course is right for you.

The foundation programme would suit:

As a student on the course, you will be a full member of the University, enjoying access to the Students’ Union, clubs, societies, sports facilities and support departments, and the outstanding student experience Loughborough University offers.

This course is placed within the Business and Humanities stream which is one of our four Foundation streams. Foundation courses in this stream include:

More information on our four Foundation streams can be found here

Why complete a foundation year

The Foundation Studies course also offers the opportunity for students performing at a very high standard in their chosen sport, looking to join one of our sporting performance programmes, who wish to study at Loughborough, but do not have the required qualifications. It is ideal for students who wish to combine their performance sports training with academic study. If you think your sport profile qualifies you to be considered for the elite athletes programme, please contact performancesport@lboro.ac.uk before applying.

[15].course_overview: Develop the skills you need to become a business analyst, or to work in the growing range of analytics-related business and management roles emerging worldwide, on this sector-leading degree at Loughborough Business School. With an optional placement opportunity, you will be able to apply what you learn in class to real-world settings and gain valuable work experience to supercharge your future career.

Analytics is used all around us. The World Economic Forum predicts that data analytics will be the main driver of the Fourth Industrial Revolution, impacting all sectors of the economy. Our BSc in Business Analytics gives you a thorough understanding of the opportunities and challenges brought by data-driven, evidence-based decision making in organisations and industries. You will also learn how to integrate specialist knowledge with general business and management skills.

This is a challenging but rewarding programme and is open to students who have not studied maths at A level or equivalent. You will benefit from extensive support both inside and outside the lecture room, helping you to build confidence and get the most from your studies.

[15].course_content_by_year[0].modules[3].description: The aims of this module are: to prepare students with a sound foundation of information and digital business for subsequent information management modules; to prepare students for further information management modules in their second and final years; to prepare students for their Industrial and Professional Studies placements; to develop relevant transferable skills.
[15].course_content_by_year[0].modules[4].title: Management and International Business Fundamentals
[15].course_content_by_year[0].modules[4].description: The aims of this module are to: prepare students with a foundation of various management perspectives and concepts; Examine some of the local, national and international factors and actors which impact businesses and organisations; gain an understanding of the complexity of doing business in the international business environment; develop an understanding of how managers and workers work individually, in groups and in teams within organisations; encourage an openness to new ideas and an awareness that in many situations there are a range of alternative perspectives that might be taken and courses of action that should be evaluated.
[15].course_content_by_year[0].modules[5].title: Principles of Business Analytics
[15].course_content_by_year[0].modules[5].description: The aims of this module are to: explore the origins and concepts of business analytics; examine the position and role of the business analyst in the organisation; explore business analytics within a range of exciting contemporary contexts.
[15].course_content_by_year[0].modules[6].title: Ethics and Professional Skills
[15].course_content_by_year[0].modules[6].description: The aims of this module are to: explore the origins and concepts of ethical business in practice; examine ethical dilemmas from a range of exciting contemporary contexts; develop expertise in collaborative project work, professional skills and preparedness for the world of work.
[15].course_content_by_year[0].modules[7].title: Programming Fundamentals
[15].course_content_by_year[0].modules[7].description: Modern firms rely on advanced programming and data analytics. This module is an introduction to the topic of programming business systems that aims to build a base level of knowledge that can then be taken forward in further learning beyond the module. Through this, students will be able to understand and practice a core capability of modern firms, especially technology firms. The module will give a base level of understanding of Machine Learning, Artificial Intelligence, and general Data Analytics.
[15].course_content_by_year[0].modules[8].title: International Business and Culture in Different Contexts
[15].course_content_by_year[0].modules[8].description: This module offers a comprehensive introduction to the field of comparative and cross-cultural management. It aims to guide students with diverse types of business and management systems around the world with a specific focus on cross-cultural differences at the national level. It will provide a critical analysis of issues and assumptions underlying various approaches to studying national cultures and equip students with cross-cultural understandings and attitudes to manage the core aspects of cross-cultural management.
[15].course_content_by_year[0].modules[9].title: Introduction to Accounting
[15].course_content_by_year[0].modules[9].description: The aims of this module are to: provide an introduction to financial accounting, its key concepts and context; develop students' skills in preparing and interpreting financial statements; explore the subjective nature of financial reporting, its benefits and its limitations; develop students' analytical and written presentational skills; develop and enhance transferable skills.
[15].course_content_by_year[0].modules[10].title: Organisational Behaviour
[15].course_content_by_year[0].modules[10].description: The aims of this module are prepare students with a sound foundation of behavioural and organisational concepts for subsequent management modules; develop an understanding of individual, group, and organisational characteristics and processes and their influence on organisational outcomes; develop an understanding of contextual influences on individuals and groups at work.
[15].course_content_by_year[0].modules[11].title: Principles of Finance
[15].course_content_by_year[0].modules[11].description: The aims of this module are: to provide an introduction to core issues in corporate finance; to provide an understanding of how corporate finance relates to other corporate managerial activities; to develop relevant transferable skills.
[15].course_content_by_year[0].modules[12].title: Principles of Law
[15].course_content_by_year[0].modules[12].description: The aims of this module are: to introduce basic legal concepts relevant to commercial activity, and to explain their relevance as a parameter of business decision-making. to explain how legal principles are created by both case law and statute, to illustrate their relevance to all aspects of business activity.

[15].course_content_by_year[1].modules[1].title: Operations and Supply Chain Management
[15].course_content_by_year[1].modules[1].description: The aims of this module are to: provide an understanding of the operations and supply chain management function and its role in organisations; introduce students to the key issues and techniques for effective operations and supply chain management; have an appreciation of the emerging trends and new technology in operations and supply chain management.
[15].course_content_by_year[1].modules[2].title: The Future Workplace
[15].course_content_by_year[1].modules[2].description: The aims of this module are to: explore current and future development in the workplace; examine the future of work within a range of exciting contemporary contexts; develop expertise in employability skills and preparedness for the future workplace, including internships and Part I placements/study abroad.
[15].course_content_by_year[1].modules[3].title: Management Science Methods
[15].course_content_by_year[1].modules[3].description: The aims of this module are: to ensure that students have an understanding of key principles, models and techniques used to tackle management decision problems; to develop skills in the analysis and modelling of management situations and approaches to evaluation and assessment of alternatives in complex scenarios; to develop core concepts and skills required to effectively support managers faced with decision problems.
[15].course_content_by_year[1].modules[4].title: Grassroots Business
[15].course_content_by_year[1].modules[4].description: The aims of this module are to: examine the factors that influence prosperity and success of local communities from a business perspective; enable students to articulate the importance and contribution of local community economies.
[15].course_content_by_year[1].modules[5].title: Business Information Management
[15].course_content_by_year[1].modules[5].description: The aims of this module are: to provide students with the basic information management and information systems knowledge and skills relevant to managers; to build on the first year skills module, to prepare students for further IT modules in semester 2 and/or in their final year; to provide students with a framework within which they can analyse the information and IT needs of businesses; to prepare students for their Industrial and Professional Studies placements; to develop relevant transferable skills.
[15].course_content_by_year[1].modules[6].title: Digital Technologies for Accounting and Finance
[15].course_content_by_year[1].modules[6].description: The aims of this module are to: develop a broad spectrum of digital techniques and big data analytical skills applicable to real-life problem-solving associated with the accounting and finance professions; explore unstructured data and its application in accounting and finance; encourage an openness to new ideas and awareness that, in many situations, there is a range of alternatives which should be evaluated; develop relevant transferable skills.
[15].course_content_by_year[1].modules[7].title: Financial Markets and Derivatives Fundamentals
[15].course_content_by_year[1].modules[7].description: The aims of this module are: to introduce the roles, functions and operations of secondary capital (equity and bond) and commodity markets and the foreign exchange market; to develop an understanding of the financial risks firms are exposed to in these markets and related positions and instruments; to provide an introduction to the methods and derivatives that may be used to hedge risk exposures, and by traders and speculators to profit in these markets.
[15].course_content_by_year[1].modules[8].title: Marketing
[15].course_content_by_year[1].modules[8].description: The aims of this module are: to introduce students to the concepts, principles and techniques involved in marketing; to familiarise students with the role of marketing management within organisations (including retail, consumer goods, industrial goods, service, non-profit oriented) and across international contexts.
[15].course_content_by_year[1].modules[9].title: Transformative International Business in Practice
[15].course_content_by_year[1].modules[9].description: The module aims to deepen students' understanding of key issues and theories in international business by examining the international business environment and the globalisation megatrend. Building on the prerequisite module, this module explores the strategies and behaviours of multinational corporations (MNCs) and highlights the principal issues involved in developing international business organisations. Students will learn to apply strategic management concepts in an international context and understand the broader implications of international business within the global landscape. Additionally, the module will address recent phenomena in international business, with a focus on emerging markets and the emergence of new business models for global impact. We take a critical approach that challenges conventional norms and encourage you to delve deep into the new dimensions of international business, such as the sustainability, impact of capitalism within a racial context and the increasing engagement of Western strategic management with emerging and frontier postcolonial economies. This module lays a crucial foundation for subsequent modules in international business.
[15].course_content_by_year[1].modules[10].title: Human Resource Management
[15].course_content_by_year[1].modules[10].description: The aims of this module are: to build on the pre-requisite module; to examine critically the role of the Human Resource Management (HRM) function within the contemporary organisation; to develop a clear understanding of the role of the HRM function in maintaining an equitable relationship between employer and employee.
[15].course_content_by_year[1].modules[11].title: Organisation Studies
[15].course_content_by_year[1].modules[11].description: The aims of this module are: To develop a social scientific understanding of organisational theories, themes, concepts and practices; To encourage a challenging, questioning perspective on organisational behaviour, research and ideas.
[15].course_content_by_year[1].modules[12].title: Accounting for Management Decisions
[15].course_content_by_year[1].modules[12].description: The aims of this module are: to develop a range of technical and analytical skills appropriate to the practice of management accounting; to critically evaluate the technical aspects of management accounting as applied to a variety of organisational contexts.
[15].course_content_by_year[1].modules[13].title: University-wide Language Programme
[15].course_content_by_year[1].modules[13].description: This is a 10 credit module from the University-wide language programme.
[15].course_content_by_year[1].modules[14].title: Business Sustainability Project
[15].course_content_by_year[1].modules[14].description: The aims of this module are to: explore the concepts and frameworks of business sustainability; examine sustainability practices in a range of exciting contemporary contexts; develop expertise in collaborative project work; build resilience.
[15].course_content_by_year[1].modules[15].title: Data Analysis for Management
[15].course_content_by_year[1].modules[15].description: The aims of this module are to: further develop the concepts and skills required to use statistics to help managers in decision making; build on the prerequisite module; extend competence in the use of computer packages; develop the ability to build models to help solve management problems; develop relevant transferable skills.
[15].course_content_by_year[1].modules[16].title: Financial Statements Analysis and Valuations
[15].course_content_by_year[1].modules[16].description: The aims of this module are to: develop an understanding of, and apply, the tools of financial statements analysis to restate a set of financial statements, conduct a performance appraisal and forecast earnings; develop an understanding of, and apply, valuation tools to explore and critically evaluate valuation issues; develop spreadsheet modelling skills and prepare a professional performance and valuation appraisal report; develop and enhance transferable skills.
[15].course_content_by_year[1].modules[17].title: Company Law
[15].course_content_by_year[1].modules[17].description: The aims of this module are: to introduce the fundamental principles of company law to develop an understanding of the significance of the company within the context of commercial activity.
[15].course_content_by_year[1].modules[18].title: Corporate Social Irresponsibility and International Governance
[15].course_content_by_year[1].modules[18].description: The aims of this module are to: enable students to understand the wider political, economic, social, and cultural contexts shaping business activities; provide a deeper understanding of the corporate governance systems encountered by multinational corporations around the world; evaluate failures in corporate governance and irresponsible business practices; demonstrate the relevance of the institutional context in the adoption, adaptation and diffusion of management practices across the world; provide a deeper understanding of organisational resilience, responsibility and regeneration.
[15].course_content_by_year[1].modules[19].title: Economics for Business I
[15].course_content_by_year[1].modules[19].description: This module aims to introduce students to some of the key economic theories and policy issues at the organisational, industry and economy-wide level.
[15].course_content_by_year[1].modules[20].title: Digital Marketing
[15].course_content_by_year[1].modules[20].description: The module aims to equip students with an in-depth knowledge of the digital marketing, including social media. We will also study the underlying academic theories of marketing, business and consumer behavior and how these relate to the application of digital marketing in the real world.
[15].course_content_by_year[1].modules[21].title: University-wide Language Programme
[15].course_content_by_year[1].modules[21].description: This is a 10 credit module from the University-wide language programme.

[15].course_content_by_year[2].modules[0].description: The aims of this module are: to extend and build on pre-requisite modules in Marketing, Accounting, and Human Resource Management; to develop an appreciation of how organisations act strategically at the business level; to encourage an openness to new ideas and an awareness that in many situations there is a range of options which should be evaluated; to develop an appreciation of the global and local contexts in which strategy is formed; to develop the ability to think critically about overarching strategic concepts.
[15].course_content_by_year[2].modules[1].title: Small Business Issues and Planning
[15].course_content_by_year[2].modules[1].description: The aims of this module are to: develop student understanding of a range of issues affecting small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs); build on these issues and put theory into practice through the creation of a business plan for a real or imaginary business; develop relevant transferable skills and understanding of how organisations start and grow in preparation for graduate employment.
[15].course_content_by_year[2].modules[2].title: Strategic Management of Big Data
[15].course_content_by_year[2].modules[2].description: The aims of this module are to: develop a critical appreciation of the theory and practice of managing big data and its significance for business and other organisations in the global environment; develop an awareness of the skills required for managing big data; understand how big data can be used to address real-world issues; understand how business opportunities can be identified and exploited using big data; explore the range of software tools available for managing large data sets.
[15].course_content_by_year[2].modules[3].title: Advanced Analytics for Web and Social Media
[15].course_content_by_year[2].modules[3].description: The aims of this module are to: provide students with web and social media analytics skills and technical knowledge relevant to business operations and managers; build on the second-year data and analytics skills; provide students with a framework within which they can analyse web-based content and systems; develop relevant transferable skills.
[15].course_content_by_year[2].modules[4].title: Decision and Efficiency Analysis
[15].course_content_by_year[2].modules[4].description: The aims of the module are to: develop an understanding of the complex multidimensional nature of decision and efficiency analysis problems faced by managers and policy makers; develop skills in modelling decision and efficiency analysis problems; obtain hands-on experience with the use of computers for decision and efficiency analysis in a business or policy environment; demonstrate the usefulness of decision and efficiency analysis in a global economic context; examine the societal and ethical implications of decision and efficiency analysis.
[15].course_content_by_year[2].modules[5].title: Entrepreneurship and Innovation
[15].course_content_by_year[2].modules[5].description: This module aims to equip students with an applied understanding of entrepreneurs and their activities in a wide range of contemporary settings.
[15].course_content_by_year[2].modules[6].title: Financial Risk Management
[15].course_content_by_year[2].modules[6].description: The aim of this module is for students to extend their knowledge of derivatives to pricing models and to credit derivatives. It covers the application of derivatives to risk management in domestic and international markets and looks at the risks of using derivatives.
[15].course_content_by_year[2].modules[7].title: Corporate Governance
[15].course_content_by_year[2].modules[7].description: The aims of this module are: To provide an introduction to corporate governance in the UK; To provide an understanding of different governance mechanisms; To develop relevant transferable skills
[15].course_content_by_year[2].modules[8].title: Sales Management
[15].course_content_by_year[2].modules[8].description: The aim of this module is to introduce students to the principles and techniques of personal selling and sales management in industrial and consumer marketing.
[15].course_content_by_year[2].modules[9].title: Advanced Interpersonal Skills
[15].course_content_by_year[2].modules[9].description: The aims of this module are: To develop an in-depth understanding of the key interpersonal skills needed for effective management of self and others in organisations from both a theoretical and practical perspective. To enable students to reflect on their current range, and level of interpersonal skills and identify areas for further development. To draw upon students relevant work experience. To consider how these skills may affect their future roles as managers, consultants or researchers. To develop relevant transferable skills.
[15].course_content_by_year[2].modules[10].title: International Human Resource Management
[15].course_content_by_year[2].modules[10].description: The aims of this module are: to build on previous Human Resource Management modules; to examine critically the role of the Human Resource Management (HRM) in an international context.
[15].course_content_by_year[2].modules[11].title: Contemporary Issues in Marketing
[15].course_content_by_year[2].modules[11].description: The module aims to address relevant and contemporary issues in marketing that shape customer experience and value creation (contemporary issues in marketing could include branding, artificial intelligence, neuromarketing, ethics and sustainability, omni channel retailing or the sharing economy).
[15].course_content_by_year[2].modules[12].title: International Marketing
[15].course_content_by_year[2].modules[12].description: This module is designed to develop an appreciation of the special requirements for successfully conducting international marketing activities by concentrating on the market-oriented approach to doing international business. Overall, the aims of this module are to build on students' knowledge of basic marketing, to present the key concepts and core issues in international marketing, and to develop decision-making skills for the successful formulation, implementation and control of international marketing programmes. Student learning objectives are to: secure knowledge of international marketing theory (e.g., the theoretical frameworks designed to assist in the making of foreign market entry decisions); develop an understanding of this theory (e.g., be able to explain the fundamental differences between the various global marketing pricing policies); show you would be able to apply them (e.g., selecting the correct theories or frameworks to be applied when making international marketing decisions, and using the theories in a way that enhances the decision-making activity).
[15].course_content_by_year[2].modules[13].title: Organisational Intelligence
[15].course_content_by_year[2].modules[13].description: The aims of the module are: to develop a critical understanding of the principles, practices and theories of information and knowledge management, and their application in the workplace; for the student to explore current developments in, and issues relating to, information and knowledge management as it applies to workplace practice; to develop understanding of the importance and impact of knowledge sharing in global organisations, and an appreciation of how one may develop an organisational culture favourable to knowledge sharing.
[15].course_content_by_year[2].modules[14].title: University-wide Language Programme
[15].course_content_by_year[2].modules[14].description: This is a 10 credit module from the University-wide language programme.
[15].course_content_by_year[2].modules[15].title: Work-Based Project
[15].course_content_by_year[2].modules[15].description: The aims of this module are to: draw together, focus on and apply specific aspects of the programme; explore and apply research methods; examine a chosen organisation at depth; develop expertise in presenting analysis, findings and recommendations.
[15].course_content_by_year[2].modules[16].title: Data Management and Visualisation
[15].course_content_by_year[2].modules[16].description: The aims of this module are to: prepare students with a thorough understanding of database management systems, and the data structures and algorithms used to represent and manipulate data effectively; build on the second year modules which introduced database systems and on students' experience of working with such systems during the industrial and professional studies year; develop relevant transferable skills.
[15].course_content_by_year[2].modules[17].title: Multinational Financial Management
[15].course_content_by_year[2].modules[17].description: The aims of this module are to: build on the pre-requisite modules develop an understanding of the practice of financial management in companies operating in the international environment develop an understanding of balance of payment dynamics, international capital flows and nature of currency attacks develop critical reasoning skills in the context of international financial risk management. This course explores managing international business and global competition with an understanding of international financial instruments, markets and institutions.
[15].course_content_by_year[2].modules[18].title: Business Optimisation
[15].course_content_by_year[2].modules[18].description: The aims of this module are to: develop the ability to build models to help managers optimise a range of business processes and decisions; further develop the concepts and skills required to a software use to help managers in decision making.
[15].course_content_by_year[2].modules[19].title: Business Forecasting
[15].course_content_by_year[2].modules[19].description: The aims of this module are: to develop an understanding of various approaches to Business Forecasting and explore their use in practice with standard IT based packages; to develop skills in analysis and modelling of management situations and a sophisticated approach to evaluation and assessment of alternatives in complex scenarios.
[15].course_content_by_year[2].modules[20].title: Behavioural Finance
[15].course_content_by_year[2].modules[20].description: The aims of this module are to: provide an understanding of mathematical models of behavioural foundations of financial decisions; develop skills that will enable students to critically analyse financial decisions in greater depth; deepen and broaden students' conceptual understanding of how financial markets 'actually work' and how people 'actually make decisions' using real-life cases and experimental results.
[15].course_content_by_year[2].modules[21].title: International Economics
[15].course_content_by_year[2].modules[21].description: The aims of this module are: to explain how and why exposure to the global economy affects domestic economic outcomes; to explain the causes and welfare consequences of international trade and trade policies; to evaluate policies towards international trade and economic integration, and how these impact businesses.
[15].course_content_by_year[2].modules[22].title: Entrepreneurship in Postconflict Spaces
[15].course_content_by_year[2].modules[22].description: This module aims to address the opportunities and challenges presented to capitalism as new markets emerge in postconflict spaces. It assesses the extent to which capitalism can engage with postconflict places, and critically reviews the problems of applying Western ways to non-Western systems.
[15].course_content_by_year[2].modules[23].title: Strategic Information Management
[15].course_content_by_year[2].modules[23].description: The aims of this module are: to provide an understanding of: the strategic importance of information systems (IS) and information technology (IT), to provide an understanding of the strategic importance of information systems (IS) and information technology (IT) and their linkages to the overall business strategy, how IS/IT strategies are formulated, how organising and resourcing options are developed and assessed, and how business value through IT is achieved; to build on students' previous modules which introduced strategic analysis, new and emerging technologies and applications of IT, and on students' experiences of working with such systems during their academic studies, industrial placements and professional studies year.
[15].course_content_by_year[2].modules[24].title: Digital Technology and Social Justice
[15].course_content_by_year[2].modules[24].description: The aims of this module are to explore current developments in, and issues relating to, digital information and technology that increasingly shape our everyday lives and work, and to develop a critical understanding of digital technology from the perspective of social justice.
[15].course_content_by_year[2].modules[25].title: Analysing Careers
[15].course_content_by_year[2].modules[25].description: The aims of this module are: to enhance students' ability to critically assess the validity and relevance of career theory and research in contemporary workplaces; to enable students to analyse their own careers and those of other people and consequently manage them in a better-informed way; to build on the pre-requisite modules in human resource management and related areas; and on placement year experience.
[15].course_content_by_year[2].modules[26].title: Rethinking Leadership: Theory and Practice
[15].course_content_by_year[2].modules[26].description: The aim of this module is to examine the roles of leadership in contributing to organisational and individual outcomes, as well as preparing students for their development into leadership roles.
[15].course_content_by_year[2].modules[27].title: Marketing Strategy and Planning
[15].course_content_by_year[2].modules[27].description: The aims of this module are to: build on pre-requisite modules and students' experience during their Industrial and Professional Studies placement; synthesise students' understanding of marketing by exploring issues and skills in the area of strategic marketing management, and in the context of the dynamic environment in which Marketing now operates; develop relevant transferable skills.
[15].course_content_by_year[2].modules[28].title: Services Marketing
[15].course_content_by_year[2].modules[28].description: The aims of this module are to: consider the development of theories of services marketing; understand key aspects of marketing management and strategy in services; appreciate the available research evidence pertaining to the particular challenges, opportunities and strategies which are encountered by different types of service businesses
[15].course_content_by_year[2].modules[29].title: Enterprise Resource Planning
[15].course_content_by_year[2].modules[29].description: The aims of this module are: to introduce and develop the key principles of enterprise resource planning (ERP); to provide an understanding of the role of ERP systems in the effective management and integration of organisational processes; to demonstrate how ERP systems can be used to effectively model and manage supply chains; to provide hands-on experience of an industry standard ERP software, using SAP.
[15].course_content_by_year[2].modules[30].title: Project Management
[15].course_content_by_year[2].modules[30].description: The aims of this module are: to provide students with a critical theoretical and practical understanding of key topics in managing projects. to provide students with an understanding of the role of a project manager. to develop a critical appreciation of business and interpersonal skills relevant to managing projects.
[15].course_content_by_year[2].modules[31].title: University-wide Language Programme
[15].course_content_by_year[2].modules[31].description: This is a 10 credit module from the University-wide language programme.

[76].course_overview: Our BSc Management degree is a highly flexible, broad-based course that prepares you for a career in any area of business and management. Our graduates are strong communicators, adaptable and resilient to change and highly sought-after in the business world.

Today’s dynamic business environment demands the skills and confidence to operate across a range of organisational roles. This BSc Management degree will equip you with a comprehensive range of management skills and styles, and knowledge and understanding of a variety of contexts in which business decisions are made. This course aims to produce excellent managers who generate creative, sustainable solutions to business and management issues.

Most importantly, you will combine theory with practice through a range of placement pathways, including half-year or year-long work-based placements, allowing you to apply your learning in a professional setting and gain valuable industry experience.

[76].course_content_by_year[0].modules[8].title: Ethics and Professional Skills

[76].course_content_by_year[0].modules[10].description: The aims of this module are to: build on the student's principles of marketing knowledge to explore the challenges around applying marketing concepts in practice; expand the range of marketing contexts that are understood; explore case studies and real-world examples of marketing in practice.
[76].course_content_by_year[0].modules[11].title: Principles of Law

[76].course_content_by_year[1].modules[3].description: The aims of this module are: to introduce the roles, functions and operations of secondary capital (equity and bond) and commodity markets and the foreign exchange market; to develop an understanding of the financial risks firms are exposed to in these markets and related positions and instruments; to provide an introduction to the methods and derivatives that may be used to hedge risk exposures, and by traders and speculators to profit in these markets.
[76].course_content_by_year[1].modules[4].title: Business Information Management
[76].course_content_by_year[1].modules[4].description: The aims of this module are: to provide students with the basic information management and information systems knowledge and skills relevant to managers; to build on the first year skills module, to prepare students for further IT modules in semester 2 and/or in their final year; to provide students with a framework within which they can analyse the information and IT needs of businesses; to prepare students for their Industrial and Professional Studies placements; to develop relevant transferable skills.
[76].course_content_by_year[1].modules[5].title: Digital Technologies for Accounting and Finance
[76].course_content_by_year[1].modules[5].description: The aims of this module are to: develop a broad spectrum of digital techniques and big data analytical skills applicable to real-life problem-solving associated with the accounting and finance professions; explore unstructured data and its application in accounting and finance; encourage an openness to new ideas and awareness that, in many situations, there is a range of alternatives which should be evaluated; develop relevant transferable skills.
[76].course_content_by_year[1].modules[6].title: Grassroots Business
[76].course_content_by_year[1].modules[6].description: The aims of this module are to: examine the factors that influence prosperity and success of local communities from a business perspective; enable students to articulate the importance and contribution of local community economies.
[76].course_content_by_year[1].modules[7].title: Transformative International Business in Practice
[76].course_content_by_year[1].modules[7].description: The module aims to deepen students' understanding of key issues and theories in international business by examining the international business environment and the globalisation megatrend. Building on the prerequisite module, this module explores the strategies and behaviours of multinational corporations (MNCs) and highlights the principal issues involved in developing international business organisations. Students will learn to apply strategic management concepts in an international context and understand the broader implications of international business within the global landscape. Additionally, the module will address recent phenomena in international business, with a focus on emerging markets and the emergence of new business models for global impact. We take a critical approach that challenges conventional norms and encourage you to delve deep into the new dimensions of international business, such as the sustainability, impact of capitalism within a racial context and the increasing engagement of Western strategic management with emerging and frontier postcolonial economies. This module lays a crucial foundation for subsequent modules in international business.
[76].course_content_by_year[1].modules[8].title: Human Resource Management
[76].course_content_by_year[1].modules[8].description: The aims of this module are: to build on the pre-requisite module; to examine critically the role of the Human Resource Management (HRM) function within the contemporary organisation; to develop a clear understanding of the role of the HRM function in maintaining an equitable relationship between employer and employee.
[76].course_content_by_year[1].modules[9].title: Organisation Studies
[76].course_content_by_year[1].modules[9].description: The aims of this module are: To develop a social scientific understanding of organisational theories, themes, concepts and practices; To encourage a challenging, questioning perspective on organisational behaviour, research and ideas.
[76].course_content_by_year[1].modules[10].title: Accounting for Management Decisions
[76].course_content_by_year[1].modules[10].description: The aims of this module are: to develop a range of technical and analytical skills appropriate to the practice of management accounting; to critically evaluate the technical aspects of management accounting as applied to a variety of organisational contexts.

[76].course_content_by_year[1].modules[16].title: Company Law
[76].course_content_by_year[1].modules[16].description: The aims of this module are: to introduce the fundamental principles of company law to develop an understanding of the significance of the company within the context of commercial activity.

[76].course_content_by_year[1].modules[17].description: The aims of this module are to: develop an understanding of, and apply, the tools of financial statements analysis to restate a set of financial statements, conduct a performance appraisal and forecast earnings; develop an understanding of, and apply, valuation tools to explore and critically evaluate valuation issues; develop spreadsheet modelling skills and prepare a professional performance and valuation appraisal report; develop and enhance transferable skills.
[76].course_content_by_year[1].modules[18].title: Corporate Social Irresponsibility and International Governance

[76].course_content_by_year[1].modules[19].title: Economics for Business I

[76].course_content_by_year[2].modules[11].title: International Human Resource Management

[76].course_content_by_year[2].modules[12].title: International Marketing

[73].course_overview: All organisations - from start-ups and SMEs to multinational firms - operate within, and are shaped by, rapidly changing international business dynamics. This BSc International Business degree is a contemporary business studies course that focuses on the links between core business functions and their roles within the international business context.

More than ever, business graduates are expected to demonstrate cultural sensitivity and an internationally transferable skill set. By covering key management disciplines from a global perspective, the course equips you for a successful career across a wide range of business and management roles, in any sector and from any geographical location.

Unlike many similar UK courses, our BSc International Business offers an optional six month international semester in year two, as well as a year long placement, study abroad, or Year in Enterprise in year three - providing valuable global experience. These practical opportunities, combined with strong academic foundations, significantly enhance employability, with our graduates highly sought after across a wide range of business and management careers.

[73].course_content_by_year[1].modules[4].title: Transformative International Business in Practice
[73].course_content_by_year[1].modules[4].description: The module aims to deepen students' understanding of key issues and theories in international business by examining the international business environment and the globalisation megatrend. Building on the prerequisite module, this module explores the strategies and behaviours of multinational corporations (MNCs) and highlights the principal issues involved in developing international business organisations. Students will learn to apply strategic management concepts in an international context and understand the broader implications of international business within the global landscape. Additionally, the module will address recent phenomena in international business, with a focus on emerging markets and the emergence of new business models for global impact. We take a critical approach that challenges conventional norms and encourage you to delve deep into the new dimensions of international business, such as the sustainability, impact of capitalism within a racial context and the increasing engagement of Western strategic management with emerging and frontier postcolonial economies. This module lays a crucial foundation for subsequent modules in international business.

[73].course_content_by_year[1].modules[14].title: Business Sustainability Project
[73].course_content_by_year[1].modules[14].description: The aims of this module are to: explore the concepts and frameworks of business sustainability; examine sustainability practices in a range of exciting contemporary contexts; develop expertise in collaborative project work; build resilience.
[73].course_content_by_year[1].modules[15].title: Corporate Social Irresponsibility and International Governance
[73].course_content_by_year[1].modules[15].description: The aims of this module are to: enable students to understand the wider political, economic, social, and cultural contexts shaping business activities; provide a deeper understanding of the corporate governance systems encountered by multinational corporations around the world; evaluate failures in corporate governance and irresponsible business practices; demonstrate the relevance of the institutional context in the adoption, adaptation and diffusion of management practices across the world; provide a deeper understanding of organisational resilience, responsibility and regeneration.
[73].course_content_by_year[1].modules[16].title: Programming for Business Analytics
[73].course_content_by_year[1].modules[16].description: The aims of this module are: provide students with basic programming skills and techniques, focusing on structured programming principles, relevant in solving real-world challenges in business analytics prepare students with the required foundational knowledge for further learning in digital business and analytics; enable students in developing relevant transferable skills required during professional study placement, and within the industry.
[73].course_content_by_year[1].modules[17].title: Company Law
[73].course_content_by_year[1].modules[17].description: The aims of this module are: to introduce the fundamental principles of company law to develop an understanding of the significance of the company within the context of commercial activity.
[73].course_content_by_year[1].modules[18].title: Financial Statements Analysis and Valuations
[73].course_content_by_year[1].modules[18].description: The aims of this module are to: develop an understanding of, and apply, the tools of financial statements analysis to restate a set of financial statements, conduct a performance appraisal and forecast earnings; develop an understanding of, and apply, valuation tools to explore and critically evaluate valuation issues; develop spreadsheet modelling skills and prepare a professional performance and valuation appraisal report; develop and enhance transferable skills.
[73].course_content_by_year[1].modules[19].title: Economics for Business I
[73].course_content_by_year[1].modules[19].description: This module aims to introduce students to some of the key economic theories and policy issues at the organisational, industry and economy-wide level.
[73].course_content_by_year[1].modules[20].title: Data Analysis for Management
[73].course_content_by_year[1].modules[20].description: The aims of this module are to: further develop the concepts and skills required to use statistics to help managers in decision making; build on the prerequisite module; extend competence in the use of computer packages; develop the ability to build models to help solve management problems; develop relevant transferable skills.
[73].course_content_by_year[1].modules[21].title: Digital Marketing
[73].course_content_by_year[1].modules[21].description: The module aims to equip students with an in-depth knowledge of the digital marketing, including social media. We will also study the underlying academic theories of marketing, business and consumer behavior and how these relate to the application of digital marketing in the real world.
[73].course_content_by_year[1].modules[22].title: University-wide Language Programme
[73].course_content_by_year[1].modules[22].description: This is a 10 credit module from the University-wide language programme.
[73].course_content_by_year[1].modules[23].title: Grassroots Business
[73].course_content_by_year[1].modules[23].description: The aims of this module are to: examine the factors that influence prosperity and success of local communities from a business perspective; enable students to articulate the importance and contribution of local community economies.
[73].course_content_by_year[1].modules[24].title: The Future Workplace
[73].course_content_by_year[1].modules[24].description: The aims of this module are to: explore current and future development in the workplace; examine the future of work within a range of exciting contemporary contexts; develop expertise in employability skills and preparedness for the future workplace, including internships and Part I placements/study abroad.
[73].course_content_by_year[1].modules[25].title: Transformative International Business in Practice
[73].course_content_by_year[1].modules[25].description: The module aims to deepen students' understanding of key issues and theories in international business by examining the international business environment and the globalisation megatrend. Building on the prerequisite module, this module explores the strategies and behaviours of multinational corporations (MNCs) and highlights the principal issues involved in developing international business organisations. Students will learn to apply strategic management concepts in an international context and understand the broader implications of international business within the global landscape. Additionally, the module will address recent phenomena in international business, with a focus on emerging markets and the emergence of new business models for global impact. We take a critical approach that challenges conventional norms and encourage you to delve deep into the new dimensions of international business, such as the sustainability, impact of capitalism within a racial context and the increasing engagement of Western strategic management with emerging and frontier postcolonial economies. This module lays a crucial foundation for subsequent modules in international business.
[73].course_content_by_year[1].modules[26].title: Database Management
[73].course_content_by_year[1].modules[26].description: The aims of this module are: to provide students with a basic understanding of modelling and building database applications; to prepare students for their Industrial and Professional Studies placements; to develop relevant transferable skills.
[73].course_content_by_year[1].modules[27].title: Accounting for Management Decisions
[73].course_content_by_year[1].modules[27].description: The aims of this module are: to develop a range of technical and analytical skills appropriate to the practice of management accounting; to critically evaluate the technical aspects of management accounting as applied to a variety of organisational contexts.
[73].course_content_by_year[1].modules[28].title: Digital Technologies for Accounting and Finance
[73].course_content_by_year[1].modules[28].description: The aims of this module are to: develop a broad spectrum of digital techniques and big data analytical skills applicable to real-life problem-solving associated with the accounting and finance professions; explore unstructured data and its application in accounting and finance; encourage an openness to new ideas and awareness that, in many situations, there is a range of alternatives which should be evaluated; develop relevant transferable skills.
[73].course_content_by_year[1].modules[29].title: Human Resource Management
[73].course_content_by_year[1].modules[29].description: The aims of this module are: to build on the pre-requisite module; to examine critically the role of the Human Resource Management (HRM) function within the contemporary organisation; to develop a clear understanding of the role of the HRM function in maintaining an equitable relationship between employer and employee.
[73].course_content_by_year[1].modules[30].title: Organisation Studies
[73].course_content_by_year[1].modules[30].description: The aims of this module are: To develop a social scientific understanding of organisational theories, themes, concepts and practices; To encourage a challenging, questioning perspective on organisational behaviour, research and ideas.
[73].course_content_by_year[1].modules[31].title: Global Brand Management
[73].course_content_by_year[1].modules[31].description: The aims of this module are: to build on the foundation provided by the prerequisite marketing module; to develop the knowledge and skills needed for a career in marketing and management, in particular the knowledge and skills required of a global brand manager; to encourage enthusiasm and self-motivation.

This is intended to be of benefit for both professional and academic advancement.

[73].course_content_by_year[2].modules[1].title: Global Strategic Management
[73].course_content_by_year[2].modules[1].description: The aims of this module are: to extend and build on pre-requisite modules in Marketing, Accounting, and Human Resource Management; to develop an appreciation of how organisations act strategically at the business level; to encourage an openness to new ideas and an awareness that in many situations there is a range of options which should be evaluated; to develop an appreciation of the global and local contexts in which strategy is formed; to develop the ability to think critically about overarching strategic concepts.
[73].course_content_by_year[2].modules[2].title: Entrepreneurship and Innovation
[73].course_content_by_year[2].modules[2].description: This module aims to equip students with an applied understanding of entrepreneurs and their activities in a wide range of contemporary settings.
[73].course_content_by_year[2].modules[3].title: Financial Risk Management

It covers the application of derivatives to risk management in domestic and international markets and looks at the risks of using derivatives.
[73].course_content_by_year[2].modules[4].title: Corporate Governance
[73].course_content_by_year[2].modules[4].description: The aims of this module are: To provide an introduction to corporate governance in the UK; To provide an understanding of different governance mechanisms; To develop relevant transferable skills
[73].course_content_by_year[2].modules[5].title: Contemporary Issues in Marketing
[73].course_content_by_year[2].modules[5].description: The module aims to address relevant and contemporary issues in marketing that shape customer experience and value creation (contemporary issues in marketing could include branding, artificial intelligence, neuromarketing, ethics and sustainability, omni channel retailing or the sharing economy).
[73].course_content_by_year[2].modules[6].title: Sales Management
[73].course_content_by_year[2].modules[6].description: The aim of this module is to introduce students to the principles and techniques of personal selling and sales management in industrial and consumer marketing.
[73].course_content_by_year[2].modules[7].title: Decision and Efficiency Analysis
[73].course_content_by_year[2].modules[7].description: The aims of the module are to: develop an understanding of the complex multidimensional nature of decision and efficiency analysis problems faced by managers and policy makers; develop skills in modelling decision and efficiency analysis problems; obtain hands-on experience with the use of computers for decision and efficiency analysis in a business or policy environment; demonstrate the usefulness of decision and efficiency analysis in a global economic context; examine the societal and ethical implications of decision and efficiency analysis.
[73].course_content_by_year[2].modules[8].title: Business Systems
[73].course_content_by_year[2].modules[8].description: The aims of this module are: to develop an appreciation of the use of Management Information Systems in business contexts, particularly in management planning, decision-making and control; to develop a critical perspective on Information Systems within contemporary organisations and society; to build on previous modules which introduced management aspects of Information Systems and on students' experience of working with such systems during the Industrial & Professional Studies year.
[73].course_content_by_year[2].modules[9].title: Strategic Management of Big Data
[73].course_content_by_year[2].modules[9].description: The aims of this module are to: develop a critical appreciation of the theory and practice of managing big data and its significance for business and other organisations in the global environment; develop an awareness of the skills required for managing big data; understand how big data can be used to address real-world issues; understand how business opportunities can be identified and exploited using big data; explore the range of software tools available for managing large data sets.
[73].course_content_by_year[2].modules[10].title: Advanced Interpersonal Skills
[73].course_content_by_year[2].modules[10].description: The aims of this module are: To develop an in-depth understanding of the key interpersonal skills needed for effective management of self and others in organisations from both a theoretical and practical perspective. To enable students to reflect on their current range, and level of interpersonal skills and identify areas for further development. To draw upon students relevant work experience. To consider how these skills may affect their future roles as managers, consultants or researchers. To develop relevant transferable skills.
[73].course_content_by_year[2].modules[11].title: International Human Resource Management
[73].course_content_by_year[2].modules[11].description: The aims of this module are: to build on previous Human Resource Management modules; to examine critically the role of the Human Resource Management (HRM) in an international context.
[73].course_content_by_year[2].modules[12].title: International Marketing
[73].course_content_by_year[2].modules[12].description: This module is designed to develop an appreciation of the special requirements for successfully conducting international marketing activities by concentrating on the market-oriented approach to doing international business. Overall, the aims of this module are to build on students' knowledge of basic marketing, to present the key concepts and core issues in international marketing, and to develop decision-making skills for the successful formulation, implementation and control of international marketing programmes. Student learning objectives are to: secure knowledge of international marketing theory (e.g., the theoretical frameworks designed to assist in the making of foreign market entry decisions); develop an understanding of this theory (e.g., be able to explain the fundamental differences between the various global marketing pricing policies); show you would be able to apply them (e.g., selecting the correct theories or frameworks to be applied when making international marketing decisions, and using the theories in a way that enhances the decision-making activity).
[73].course_content_by_year[2].modules[13].title: Organisational Intelligence
[73].course_content_by_year[2].modules[13].description: The aims of the module are: to develop a critical understanding of the principles, practices and theories of information and knowledge management, and their application in the workplace; for the student to explore current developments in, and issues relating to, information and knowledge management as it applies to workplace practice; to develop understanding of the importance and impact of knowledge sharing in global organisations, and an appreciation of how one may develop an organisational culture favourable to knowledge sharing.
[73].course_content_by_year[2].modules[14].title: Advanced Analytics for Web and Social Media
[73].course_content_by_year[2].modules[14].description: The aims of this module are to: provide students with web and social media analytics skills and technical knowledge relevant to business operations and managers; build on the second-year data and analytics skills; provide students with a framework within which they can analyse web-based content and systems; develop relevant transferable skills.
[73].course_content_by_year[2].modules[15].title: University-wide Language Programme
[73].course_content_by_year[2].modules[15].description: This is a 10 credit module from the University-wide language programme.
[73].course_content_by_year[2].modules[16].title: Work-Based Project
[73].course_content_by_year[2].modules[16].description: The aims of this module are to: draw together, focus on and apply specific aspects of the programme; explore and apply research methods; examine a chosen organisation at depth; develop expertise in presenting analysis, findings and recommendations.
[73].course_content_by_year[2].modules[17].title: International Negotiations
[73].course_content_by_year[2].modules[17].description: The aims of this module are to: build on prior International Business and International Management modules; create an understanding of the science, art, psychology and strategy of international negotiations; demonstrate the challenges of culture in international negotiations; evaluate the impact of strategy on negotiation processes and outcomes; appraise the relevance of concepts and theories of negotiations in an international context.
[73].course_content_by_year[2].modules[18].title: Multinational Financial Management
[73].course_content_by_year[2].modules[18].description: The aims of this module are to: build on the pre-requisite modules develop an understanding of the practice of financial management in companies operating in the international environment develop an understanding of balance of payment dynamics, international capital flows and nature of currency attacks develop critical reasoning skills in the context of international financial risk management. This course explores managing international business and global competition with an understanding of international financial instruments, markets and institutions.
[73].course_content_by_year[2].modules[19].title: Behavioural Finance
[73].course_content_by_year[2].modules[19].description: The aims of this module are to: provide an understanding of mathematical models of behavioural foundations of financial decisions; develop skills that will enable students to critically analyse financial decisions in greater depth; deepen and broaden students' conceptual understanding of how financial markets 'actually work' and how people 'actually make decisions' using real-life cases and experimental results.
[73].course_content_by_year[2].modules[20].title: International Economics
[73].course_content_by_year[2].modules[20].description: The aims of this module are: to explain how and why exposure to the global economy affects domestic economic outcomes; to explain the causes and welfare consequences of international trade and trade policies; to evaluate policies towards international trade and economic integration, and how these impact businesses.
[73].course_content_by_year[2].modules[21].title: Entrepreneurship in Postconflict Spaces
[73].course_content_by_year[2].modules[21].description: This module aims to address the opportunities and challenges presented to capitalism as new markets emerge in postconflict spaces. It assesses the extent to which capitalism can engage with postconflict places, and critically reviews the problems of applying Western ways to non-Western systems.
[73].course_content_by_year[2].modules[22].title: Strategic Information Management
[73].course_content_by_year[2].modules[22].description: The aims of this module are: to provide an understanding of: the strategic importance of information systems (IS) and information technology (IT), to provide an understanding of the strategic importance of information systems (IS) and information technology (IT) and their linkages to the overall business strategy, how IS/IT strategies are formulated, how organising and resourcing options are developed and assessed, and how business value through IT is achieved; to build on students' previous modules which introduced strategic analysis, new and emerging technologies and applications of IT, and on students' experiences of working with such systems during their academic studies, industrial placements and professional studies year.
[73].course_content_by_year[2].modules[23].title: Digital Technology and Social Justice
[73].course_content_by_year[2].modules[23].description: The aims of this module are to explore current developments in, and issues relating to, digital information and technology that increasingly shape our everyday lives and work, and to develop a critical understanding of digital technology from the perspective of social justice.
[73].course_content_by_year[2].modules[24].title: Analysing Careers
[73].course_content_by_year[2].modules[24].description: The aims of this module are: to enhance students' ability to critically assess the validity and relevance of career theory and research in contemporary workplaces; to enable students to analyse their own careers and those of other people and consequently manage them in a better-informed way; to build on the pre-requisite modules in human resource management and related areas; and on placement year experience.
[73].course_content_by_year[2].modules[25].title: Rethinking Leadership: Theory and Practice
[73].course_content_by_year[2].modules[25].description: The aim of this module is to examine the roles of leadership in contributing to organisational and individual outcomes, as well as preparing students for their development into leadership roles.
[73].course_content_by_year[2].modules[26].title: Services Marketing
[73].course_content_by_year[2].modules[26].description: The aims of this module are to: consider the development of theories of services marketing; understand key aspects of marketing management and strategy in services; appreciate the available research evidence pertaining to the particular challenges, opportunities and strategies which are encountered by different types of service businesses
[73].course_content_by_year[2].modules[27].title: Enterprise Resource Planning
[73].course_content_by_year[2].modules[27].description: The aims of this module are: to introduce and develop the key principles of enterprise resource planning (ERP); to provide an understanding of the role of ERP systems in the effective management and integration of organisational processes; to demonstrate how ERP systems can be used to effectively model and manage supply chains; to provide hands-on experience of an industry standard ERP software, using SAP.
[73].course_content_by_year[2].modules[28].title: Business Optimisation
[73].course_content_by_year[2].modules[28].description: The aims of this module are to: develop the ability to build models to help managers optimise a range of business processes and decisions; further develop the concepts and skills required to a software use to help managers in decision making.
[73].course_content_by_year[2].modules[29].title: Business Forecasting
[73].course_content_by_year[2].modules[29].description: The aims of this module are: to develop an understanding of various approaches to Business Forecasting and explore their use in practice with standard IT based packages; to develop skills in analysis and modelling of management situations and a sophisticated approach to evaluation and assessment of alternatives in complex scenarios.
[73].course_content_by_year[2].modules[30].title: Data Management and Visualisation
[73].course_content_by_year[2].modules[30].description: The aims of this module are to: prepare students with a thorough understanding of database management systems, and the data structures and algorithms used to represent and manipulate data effectively; build on the second year modules which introduced database systems and on students' experience of working with such systems during the industrial and professional studies year; develop relevant transferable skills.
[73].course_content_by_year[2].modules[31].title: Project Management
[73].course_content_by_year[2].modules[31].description: The aims of this module are: to provide students with a critical theoretical and practical understanding of key topics in managing projects. to provide students with an understanding of the role of a project manager. to develop a critical appreciation of business and interpersonal skills relevant to managing projects.

[73].course_content_by_year[2].modules[32].description: This is a 10 credit module from the University-wide language programme.

[0].course_overview: This course is primarily for candidates who have not studied the prerequisite subjects needed for first year entry, or have not met their expected entrance requirements due to adverse situations, or because of their previous sport performance commitments, as well as mature students returning to education or care leavers.

Our Foundation Studies programme at Loughborough is designed to help a range of students realise their university ambitions. Our streamed approach enables you to progress on to one of multiple courses within your chosen stream – giving you further time to decide which course is right for you.

The foundation programme would suit:

As a student on the course, you will be a full member of the University, enjoying access to the Students’ Union, clubs, societies, sports facilities and support departments, and the outstanding student experience Loughborough University offers.

This course is placed within the Engineering, Mathematics and Physical Sciences stream which is one of our four Foundation streams. Foundation courses in this stream include:

Why complete a foundation year

The Foundation Studies course also offers the opportunity for students performing at a very high standard in their chosen sport, looking to join one of our sporting performance programmes, who wish to study at Loughborough, but do not have the required qualifications. It is ideal for students who wish to combine their performance sports training with academic study. If you think your sport profile qualifies you to be considered for the elite athletes programme, please contact performancesport@lboro.ac.uk before applying.
