evidence.title: Returner Accomodation Faqs
evidence.text:
sections[2].faqs[4].answer: DASH accredited landlords should allow you at least 48 hours in which to seek advice on the proposed contract; if your prospective landlord / agents are not part of the DASH scheme, it is still reasonable for you to ask for the same period. Other students may be interested in the property and potentially there may be the risk that a delay will mean that the property is rented to others. It is important however that you make the right rather than a rushed decision. It is worth remembering that agents work for landlords and therefore it is in their clients’ best interests rather than yours that you sign. Take the time you need. Make sure you #RentSMART and understand the details in your contract, your rights and responsibilities and any risks associated with signing up early. Before you sign or pay any money: • Check out SASS’s information on what to look for before signing a contract (https://www.lboro.ac.uk/services/student-services/topics/renting-off-campus-contracts/) , and • Request an appointment (https://forms.office.com/Pages/ResponsePage.aspx?id=wE8mz7iun0SQVILORFQIS6BJi5Vezs9Coi32-3OHqYtUNFhWNzdXSkE5REJXNUZYRjNKWDVYQkVWSS4u) to get your draft contract checked with an experienced SASS housing adviser.
sections[2].faqs[5].question: Can I negotiate changes to the contract ? Can I ask for any landlord commitments to be added to the contract?
sections[2].faqs[5].answer: You can ask for changes to be made to the contract, but only before the contract is signed. A contract is a two-way agreement and before you commit yourself, you can ask for anything you would like to be added or removed. We strongly recommend that any promises made to you by the landlord/agents are added to the contract. This commits the landlord to provide and confirm in writing what has been agreed. If the landlord is promising that renovation work will be carried out before you move in such as a new bathroom/kitchen, agree and add a date into the contract by which this will be completed. The Student Advice and Support Service (SASS) has more information on negotiating a tenancy agreement (https://www.lboro.ac.uk/services/student-services/topics/renting-off-campus-negotiating-a-tenancy-contract/) .
sections[2].faqs[6].question: Is it essential to have a guarantor? What is a guarantor?
sections[2].faqs[6].answer: Some landlords/agents require students to provide a guarantor. A guarantor is someone who will guarantee to pay your rent if you fail to do so. Typically, landlords/agents expect the guarantor to be based in the UK. If you are an international student then a parent who is abroad is unlikely to be accepted. If you are unable to find a UK-based guarantor, the landlord/letting agent may ask for rent in advance or a larger deposit. If you are required to provide a guarantor, we recommend: The Student Advice and Support Service (SASS) has more information on guarantors (https://www.lboro.ac.uk/services/student-services/topics/renting-off-campus-guarantors/) . • You limit your liability by ensuring the guarantor’s agreement sets out the name of the person whose rent is being guaranteed, the start and end date the agreement applies, and the amount guaranteed rather than a general commitment to pay the outstanding rent. • You and the guarantor read the tenancy agreement and the guarantor agreement before signing. There are a number of agents who do not require guarantors so it is worth shopping around if you prefer not to provide a guarantor.
sections[2].faqs[7].question: I am being asked to pay a damage/security deposit. What is this for?
sections[2].faqs[7].answer: Many landlords/agents will ask for a damage/security deposit as part of the contract. Under the law, the amount of deposit set by landlords/agents cannot exceed the equivalent of 5 weeks’ rent. At the end of the contract, the landlord/ agent may propose deductions for any money they feel you owe. For example, damages to the property, rent arrears, or other costs such as utility debts. The contract should confirm what deductions can be made from your deposit. The Student Advice and Support Service (SASS) has more information on deposits (https://www.lboro.ac.uk/services/student-services/topics/renting-off-campus-deposit/) .
sections[2].faqs[8].question: How should my landlord / agent protect my deposit?
sections[2].faqs[8].answer: If a landlord or agent decides to take a security deposit as part of the contractual agreement with you, they must comply with the legislation which places an obligation on them to protect your deposit with one of the three government-backed schemes. This will enable you to raise a dispute with the Scheme’s adjudicator if there is a disagreement at the end of your contract about the return of your deposit. Your landlord must protect your deposit within 30 days of receipt. The landlord must also notify you within the same 30 days which scheme they have chosen, with contact details and certain other information prescribed by law. Seek advice from us if this has not been complied with. If the landlord does not correctly protect your deposit, you may be entitled to seek compensation. The Student Advice and Support Service (SASS) has more information on deposits (https://www.lboro.ac.uk/services/student-services/topics/renting-off-campus-deposit/) .
sections[2].faqs[9].question: Can I afford this property?
sections[2].faqs[9].answer: It is very important to seriously consider whether you and your housemates can all afford a property before you sign the tenancy agreement, particularly if it is a joint contract. Before you begin to look, think about what you can afford and whether you will have received your student loan when your rent is due. Remember that not all private accommodation contracts have bills included and this will be a separate expense on top of the rent that you will pay. It is likely that even if the bills are included within your housing contract, there will be a maximum amount that your landlord will pay and anything above this limit will need to be paid by you. Work out your budget using the Student Advice and Support Service resources (https://www.lboro.ac.uk/services/student-services/topics/managing-your-money/) before you commit.
sections[2].faqs[10].question: I'm being asked to sign a contract which I do not understand. Should I do this?
sections[2].faqs[10].answer: You should never sign a contract that you don't understand. It is very important to remember that a contract is a legally binding document and once you agree to the terms and conditions, it is impossible to change your mind. While it’s common for students to feel pressured by potential housemates, landlords, or agents, it is essential to take your time and ensure that you are making the right decision for yourself. Make sure you fully understand your obligations and the implications of signing the contract before you proceed. Make sure you #RentSMART and understand the details in your contract, your rights and responsibilities and any risks associated with signing up early. Before you sign or pay any money: • Check out SASS’s information on what to look for before signing a contract (https://www.lboro.ac.uk/services/student-services/topics/renting-off-campus-contracts/) , and • Request an appointment (https://forms.office.com/Pages/ResponsePage.aspx?id=wE8mz7iun0SQVILORFQIS6BJi5Vezs9Coi32-3OHqYtUNFhWNzdXSkE5REJXNUZYRjNKWDVYQkVWSS4u) to get your draft contract checked with an experienced SASS housing adviser.
sections[2].faqs[11].question: Can I change my mind later?
sections[2].faqs[11].answer: The circumstances in which you can terminate a private tenancy agreement are rare. Once you have signed an agreement, it is very unlikely that you will be able to change your mind and walk away. Any contract you sign is legally binding and becomes so even if it will be many months before you will move into the property. This is why it is incredibly important to be 100% sure that this is the right property for you before you agree. We strongly advise that you do not sign a second housing agreement whilst already committed to another one because you have changed your mind. You will be committing yourself to two contracts which you will be expected to pay for. The Student Advice and Support Service (SASS) has more information on ending your tenancy (https://www.lboro.ac.uk/services/student-services/topics/ending-your-tenancy/) .
sections[2].faqs[12].question: What help can I receive from Student Advice and Support?
sections[2].faqs[12].answer: The Student Advice and Support Service (SASS) provides a contract checking service. We can check any potential contract you are being asked to sign by a landlord/agent and we can explain the rights and responsibilities provided under the contract to you and your landlord. It is always best to have your contract checked before you pay any money or sign the agreement.
sections[2].faqs[13].question: How do I book an appointment for a contract check?
sections[2].faqs[13].answer: You can call 01509 222765 (tel:01509222765) or complete the Student Advice and Support Service online appointment request form (https://forms.office.com/Pages/ResponsePage.aspx?id=wE8mz7iun0SQVILORFQIS6BJi5Vezs9Coi32-3OHqYtUNFhWNzdXSkE5REJXNUZYRjNKWDVYQkVWSS4u) .

evidence.title: Returner Accomodation Faqs
evidence.text:
sections[1].faqs[4].question: What is my deposit for?
sections[1].faqs[4].answer: A security deposit is held until the end of the Tenancy to cover any damage. The maximum security deposit a landlord can charge is 5 weeks rent. All deposits legally must be protected by one of 3 independent deposit protection schemes. Your landlord is required to provide you with the details of which scheme they have used. The protection scheme is there to ensure all claims made by the Landlord are justified and to settle any disputes that may arise. The Student Advice and Support Service (SASS) has more information on deposits (https://www.lboro.ac.uk/services/student-services/topics/renting-off-campus-deposit/) .
sections[1].faqs[5].question: How will my rent be collected?
sections[1].faqs[5].answer: Your tenancy agreement will normally state how to pay your rent. However, there is room for negotiation, and you should ask for the method that suits you best before you sign your contract. The common methods of payment include standing order or a bank transfer. A standing order is a reliable option, as you control the payment amount and frequency through your bank, and your landlord cannot make changes to it. While direct debits are sometimes used for other services, they are not advisable for rent payments as it allows the landlord/ letting agent to withdraw money from your account, giving them control over the payment amount. The Student Advice and Support Service (SASS) has more information on living in the property (https://www.lboro.ac.uk/services/student-services/topics/renting-off-campus-living-in-the-property/) including paying rent.
sections[1].faqs[6].question: What is a guarantor?
sections[1].faqs[6].answer: Some private accommodation providers may ask for a UK based guarantor who would be liable for paying the rent for which you are responsible if for any reason you were not able to make a payment. The Student Advice and Support Service (SASS) has more information on guarantors (https://www.lboro.ac.uk/services/student-services/topics/renting-off-campus-guarantors/) .
sections[1].faqs[7].question: Will I be responsible for the bills in the property?
sections[1].faqs[7].answer: Whether you are responsible for the bills depends on the terms of your tenancy agreement. Some rental agreements include bills such as gas, electricity, water, and internet, while others do not. Make sure to check your tenancy agreement carefully to see if utilities are included. I If they are, check the cap on the included usage, as you may be charged for any consumption beyond that limit. If bills aren’t included, you will need to arrange and pay for them yourself. You will need to contact the suppliers to register on arrival at the property with the meter readings and again when leaving at the end of the tenancy. The Student Advice and Support Service (SASS) has more information on utilities (https://www.lboro.ac.uk/services/student-services/topics/renting-off-campus-utilities/) .
sections[1].faqs[8].question: Will I have to pay council tax?
sections[1].faqs[8].answer: Properties occupied by full-time students are exempt from paying council tax. You can download a ‘Council Tax letter’ from the Student Self-service portal (https://www.lboro.ac.uk/students/enquiries/self-service/) for this purpose. If you are a Loughborough London student a ‘Council Tax letter’ can be requested in person from the Student Services Desk at the London campus, or by email to: london-enquiries@lboro.ac.uk You will then need to supply this to Charnwood Borough Council (http://www.charnwood.gov.uk/pages/counciltax) or your landlord. If any of the tenants in the house are working, check how this could affect the exemption with Charnwood Borough Council. If only one tenant is working, they should be able to claim a single occupier discount, providing that all the other occupants are exempt. Please note, if your studies are part-time you may b e liable for council tax. If you are living in a property before your course commences, or after it finishes, you may find yourself billed for council tax for the period that you are not a student.
sections[1].faqs[9].question: Will I need to arrange contents insurance?
sections[1].faqs[9].answer: Yes - you will need to arrange suitable insurance cover for your own personal belongings. Your landlord will have insurance cover for the property itself and his/her contents only.
sections[1].faqs[10].question: Will the property be cleaned before my arrival?
sections[1].faqs[10].answer: The property should be clean and in good condition when you move in. If you are unhappy with its condition or notice any damage, inform your landlord immediately and note it on the inventory. It is also a good idea to take photographs, which can be useful in case of any disputes over damage or cleanliness when your tenancy ends.
sections[1].faqs[11].question: Do I need a TV Licence for each television in the house?
sections[1].faqs[11].answer: You will need a TV licence if you have a separate Tenancy Agreement for your individual room. If you have a Joint tenancy with the other occupiers of the property - only one TV Licence (http://www.tvlicensing.co.uk/) is required irrespective of how many televisions there are in the house. If you have a joint tenancy and your landlord has provided a television in your house, they may have also provided the TV licence. You should check if this is the case, as this licence would also cover any additional televisions. For further information about who requires a licence and how to apply please visit TV Licencing (http://www.tvlicensing.co.uk/check-if-you-need-one/for-your-home/students-aud1?WT.mc_id=r107&x=0) or contact 0300 790 6090. It may be possible to claim a partial refund for the Summer holiday period if you are not renting for that period. The maximum fine is £1000 for not having a licence.
sections[1].faqs[12].question: Who do I contact if I have a problem?
sections[1].faqs[12].answer: Any problems should initially be raised directly with your landlord. The Student Advice and Support Service s (http://www.lboro.ac.uk/services/sass/) offers advice on renting off campus (https://www.lboro.ac.uk/services/student-services/topics/moving-in-living-in-property/) including disrepair, problems with your landlord etc. Please also contact the Student Accommodation Centre if you experience any problems in relating to a property advertised on Studentpad.
sections[1].faqs[13].question: What support is there for me if I live off campus?
sections[1].faqs[13].answer: There is a Community Warden (https://www.lboro.ac.uk/services/community-wardens/) team that is set up to support students who live off campus. They offer help and advice about living as part of the wider community. You are able to still be affiliated with a hall of residence and live off campus. For information about how you can get involved in Hall committee arranged social programmes visit the LSU website (https://lsu.co.uk/halls) .
sections[2].section_title: Student Advice and Support Services
sections[2].faqs[0].question: What should I consider when house hunting?
sections[2].faqs[0].answer: The Student Advice and Support Service have a Renting off campus guide (https://www.lboro.ac.uk/services/student-services/topics/renting-off-campus-house-hunting/) which includes what to consider when house hunting. You can use their viewing a property checklist (https://www.lboro.ac.uk/services/student-services/topics/viewing-a-property/) to compare properties
sections[2].faqs[1].question: Is it OK to sign the contract if my friends have viewed the property and I haven’t?
sections[2].faqs[1].answer: We highly advise that you visit the accommodation in person before agreeing to move in or sign any agreements. While it’s understandable to want to secure the property quickly, viewing it yourself is crucial as your friends’ impressions may differ from yours. Tenants who haven't viewed a property personally prior to signing do not have any additional cancellation rights. If you are unable to inspect the property in person, it may be best to postpone your search for accommodation until you can do so.
sections[2].faqs[2].question: How do I find a property?
sections[2].faqs[2].answer: We would encourage you to begin your search on Studentpad (https://www.loughboroughstudentpad.co.uk/Accommodation) , a website managed by the Student Accommodation Centre (SAC). All properties advertised on this site have been inspected by SAC. Landlords who advertise on the site are accredited by Decent and Safe Homes (DASH) Landlord Accreditation and meet the standards set in partnership with Charnwood Borough Council. The Student Advice and Support Service (SASS) has more information on how to find a property (https://www.lboro.ac.uk/services/student-services/topics/where-to-find-property/) .
sections[2].faqs[3].question: Some students I know have already signed a contract. Should I find somewhere quickly?
sections[2].faqs[3].answer: It is common to feel pressure from letting agents and sometimes friends to rush into signing a tenancy agreement. Whenever you choose to sign a contract make sure you #RentSMART and understand the details in your contract, your rights and responsibilities and any risks associated with signing up early. Before you sign or pay any money: • Check out SASS’s information on what to look for before signing a contract (https://www.lboro.ac.uk/services/student-services/topics/renting-off-campus-contracts/) , and • Request an appointment (https://forms.office.com/Pages/ResponsePage.aspx?id=wE8mz7iun0SQVILORFQIS6BJi5Vezs9Coi32-3OHqYtUNFhWNzdXSkE5REJXNUZYRjNKWDVYQkVWSS4u) to get your draft contract checked with an experienced SASS housing adviser.

evidence.title: Contextual Offer Faqs
evidence.text:
sections[1].faqs[6].question: Can I be made a reduced offer if I am not eligible for an Access Loughborough Contextual Offer?
sections[1].faqs[6].answer: Eligibility for an Access Loughborough Contextual Offer guarantees that if you are made an offer, it will be reduced by up to two grades. A reduced offer of up to one grade lower than typical entry requirements may occasionally be made due to other contextual information considered.
sections[1].faqs[7].question: If I am eligible for a reduced contextual offer, can I defer my place for a year?
sections[1].faqs[7].answer: Opportunities sometimes arise for students to take a gap year, either to go travelling or gain work experience. We will always try to support students who want to defer for one year and this would not affect your eligibility a reduced contextual offer. If you have decided that you want to amend your year of entry, please email the Undergraduate Admissions Office, including your full name and UCAS Personal ID Number. We will usually be able to process this change fairly swiftly and you will see an amendment to your offer on your UCAS application and receive a new offer letter stating the updated year of entry.
sections[1].faqs[8].question: Do I need to accept Loughborough as my firm or insurance offer to be eligible for a contextual offer?
sections[1].faqs[8].answer: No, you do not need to make Loughborough University your Firm or Insurance choice to be eligible for a contextual offer if you receive one.

sections[0].section_title: FAQs
sections[0].faqs[0].question: How do I become a Loughborough alumni?
sections[0].faqs[0].answer: You are an alumni by virtue of having studied at the University for more than three months and you automatically join the Loughborough University Alumni Association. This is a membership group made up of all former students, graduates and retired staff and is governed by a constitution which ensures that Loughborough graduates have a voice within the University. The Association’s members are represented by the Alumni Advisory Board (AAB), which is made up of representatives from our graduate community around the world. These representatives are democratically elected each year by our alumni population. The President of the AAB also has a seat on the University Council. This ensures that alumni are given a voice at the highest level of University decision-making.
sections[0].faqs[1].question: What are the benefits of being Loughborough alumni?
sections[0].faqs[1].answer: As alumni you can access a range of exclusive benefits (https://www.lboro.ac.uk/alumni/alumni-benefits/) , both on the high street and for university facilities, such as the Library and the sports facilities. You will also receive news in the form of our monthly e-newsletter, updates from the University and notifications of any relevant upcoming events, such as guest lectures and reunions. We have a range of ways to engage with fellow alumni and current students (https://www.lboro.ac.uk/alumni/get-involved/) through offering graduate job opportunities, mentoring current students or alumni and the chance to network with fellow members of Loughborough’s alumni and student communities.
sections[0].faqs[2].question: What if my contact details change?
sections[0].faqs[2].answer: You can update your details (https://www.lboro.ac.uk/alumni/update-details/) or contact us (https://www.lboro.ac.uk/alumni/contact-us/) directly whenever your details change so that you continue to stay in touch.
sections[0].faqs[3].question: Can I log in to the alumni website?
sections[0].faqs[3].answer: We have removed the feature which enabled you to log in to the alumni website. You can contact us at any time to find out what details we hold on you, and you can update your details without logging in. Need to know more? Read our Privacy Policy. (https://www.lboro.ac.uk/alumni/privacy-policy/)
sections[0].faqs[4].question: Can I opt out of hearing from the University?
sections[0].faqs[4].answer: You can opt out and opt back in at any time. Simply update your details (https://www.lboro.ac.uk/alumni/update-details/) or contact us (https://www.lboro.ac.uk/alumni/contact-us/) directly to let us know if you would like to stop hearing from us, or if you would like to hear from us again.
sections[0].faqs[5].question: If I lose my degree certificate and/or my degree transcript, how can I get a new one?
sections[0].faqs[5].answer: You can purchase duplicate degree certificates (https://store.lboro.ac.uk/product-catalogue/academic-registry/degree-certificates) . Duplicate degree transcripts (which list the modules you undertook and marks you received) can be bought online (https://store.lboro.ac.uk/product-catalogue/academic-registry/degree-transcripts) for those who graduated after 1996 (if you graduated in 1995 or earlier, you will need to contact the academic department at which you studied). Please note that new certificates and transcripts will usually take 2-3 weeks to be delivered to a UK destination, and 4-6 weeks to be delivered internationally. If you have special requirements, for example you would like a transcript to be sent to World Education Services in Canada or the USA, please note this in the additional information section of your order and email instructions/the accompanying paperwork to graduation@lboro.ac.uk. (mailto:graduation@lboro.ac.uk)
sections[0].faqs[6].question: How do I find out my degree results?
sections[0].faqs[6].answer: We are unable to disclose University results. However, these will be shown on your degree transcript, along with the modules you studied. You will have been provided one at your University graduation. Duplicates can be bought online (https://store.lboro.ac.uk/product-catalogue/academic-registry/degree-transcripts) provided you graduated post-1996. If you graduated in 1995 or earlier, you will need to contact the academic department at which you studied. If you have any other queries regarding results, please email (mailto:studentrecords@mailbox.lboro.ac.uk) or call the Student Records & Operations department on 01509 222491.
sections[0].faqs[7].question: How can I get involved with the University?
sections[0].faqs[7].answer: There are several ways through which you can be involved with the University (https://www.lboro.ac.uk/alumni/get-involved/) , allowing you to give back to both fellow alumni and current students. These include: • Guest lectures • Career mentoring • Offering an alumni profile • Providing graduate and placement opportunities • Being an International Ambassador Alumni skills and experience are important in helping our next generation of students. If you are interested in volunteering in any way, please do contact us (mailto:alumni@lboro.ac.uk) for more information.
sections[0].faqs[8].question: Can I keep up-to-date with the Alumni Association on social media?
sections[0].faqs[8].answer: Follow us across social media to keep up-to-date with the latest Loughborough alumni news and events. Like us on Facebook (https://www.facebook.com/lboroalumni) Follow us on X (formerly Twitter) (https://twitter.com/lboroalumni) Join our network on LinkedIn (https://www.linkedin.com/in/loughborough-alumni-374b5693/) and connect with fellow alumni
sections[0].faqs[9].question: Can I visit campus?
sections[0].faqs[9].answer: You are welcome to visit campus again once you have graduated. Whether you are coming back to see friends or wish to visit again after many years, you are welcome. Please note that car parking charges apply (https://www.lboro.ac.uk/services/fm/services/traffic-parking/visitors/) for visitors. If you wish to visit with prospective students, check out our Open Days (https://www.lboro.ac.uk/study/undergraduate/visit-us/open-days/) . If you're looking for alumni events (https://www.lboro.ac.uk/alumni/events) , see what we have coming up. Let us know (mailto:alumni@lboro.ac.uk) if you have any questions about visiting us.
sections[0].faqs[10].question: How can I reconnect with old friends?
sections[0].faqs[10].answer: Due to Data Protection, we are unable to pass on details of members of your cohort without their permission. However, if you would like to arrange a reunion or get back in touch with someone, please contact us (https://www.lboro.ac.uk/alumni/contact-us/) with short message and your contact details and we can send an email on your behalf.
sections[0].faqs[11].question: How can I access my alumni e-mail?
sections[0].faqs[11].answer: Alumni e-mail accounts (ending in @alumni.lboro.ac.uk) were deactivated in December 2017, following the University’s move from Google to Microsoft as its e-mail provider. All e-mails are sent to those which are provided to us by alumni. Feel free to update your details (https://www.lboro.ac.uk/alumni/update-details/) to make sure we can keep in touch.
sections[0].faqs[12].question: How can I access my student e-mail account and Learn pages?
sections[0].faqs[12].answer: Once you have graduated, your student e-mail account and username (ending in @student.lboro.ac.uk) enters a 30-day expiry period. During this period, you can forward or download any documents to an alternative e-mail address or location. When this 30-day period expires, the student e-mail and username will be deactivated, and will no longer be accessible. This also includes subscription to Microsoft Office. Please see the IT Services FAQs page (http://www.lboro.ac.uk/services/it/student/email/faq/) for more information.

sections[0].section_title: Using the Lboro Sport app
sections[0].faqs[0].question: I am a Loughborough University Student/Staff member and can not activate my account
sections[0].faqs[0].answer: If you can not activate your account after following our online joining process (https://www.lboro.ac.uk/sport/memberships-prices/join/) , this may be due to one of the following reasons; Your personal details are incorrect or your email address is not registered on our system, this will happen if; Please contact the sport memberships team and provide the following information for us to locate your account and assist; • We have not received confirmation of your enrolment from the University • You have previously changed your email address which differs to the email address you are trying to re-set your password with • You did a different course at the University previously, as your original student email address will remain on our system • You are a Loughborough College Student • Full Name • Date of Birth • Mobile Number • Student/Staff ID • University/College Email address
sections[0].faqs[1].question: I am a community member, how do I sign up for an account?
sections[0].faqs[1].answer: All new members will need to sign up for an account. To use our facilities on a casual basis please join as a Pay as You Go member for free. If you believe you have a registered account but can not activate this, please contact sportmemberships@lboro.ac.uk (mailto:sportmemberships@lboro.ac.uk) and provide the following information for us to locate your account and provide assistance; If you fall under our affiliate category (https://www.lboro.ac.uk/sport/memberships-prices/discount-categories/) , please ensure that you also send us proof of eligibility to reactivate your discount price. • Full name • Date of Birth • Mobile number
sections[0].faqs[2].question: I can not use the app to gain access through the barriers
sections[0].faqs[2].answer: To gain access through the barriers using your phone on our Check In tiles at Holywell, Powerbase, the Swimming Pool and HiPAC, please ensure that you have done the following; • Booked a session in the facility, the gates will not open unless a valid booking is present. • Logged into the Lboro Sport app with your credentials. • Update the Lboro Sport app to the latest version in the App Store and Google Play.
sections[0].faqs[3].question: I am being charged for a session that is included in my membership
sections[0].faqs[3].answer: If the app is charging you have an activity, please check the following; *Recent app updates now allow for members to book guests into classes. You will now see the guest price displayed on the booking page, however, if you are booking for yourself and hold a membership which includes classes this price will change to £0 once you add it to the basket and check out. • Your membership (https://www.lboro.ac.uk/sport/memberships-prices/) includes access to the activity you are trying to book at no additional charge • You are logged into the Lboro Sport app with your credentials. • Update the Lboro Sport app to the latest version in the App Store and Google Play.
sections[0].faqs[4].question: I can not reset my password I do not receive the password reset email
sections[0].faqs[4].answer: If you do not receive an email within 5 minutes of submitting the password request form, the following may apply; Your email address is not registered on our system, this will happen if; • We have not received confirmation of your enrolment from the University • You have previously changed your email address to the email address you are trying to re-set your password with • You did a different course at the University previously, as your original student email address will remain on our system
sections[0].faqs[5].question: I am trying to purchase a membership but I keep getting the error 'This Membership is already held and so can not purchase again'
sections[0].faqs[5].answer: This message will display when an attempt to purchase has been made but payment was not taken. To pay; • Go to the home screen of the Lboro Sports app • Select the tile titled My Account • Select the tile titled Bills & Payments • Log in if required • The unpaid membership subscription will display in the Bills section • Select the outstanding membership and follow the on screen instructions to proceed to payment
sections[1].section_title: Gyms
sections[1].faqs[0].question: How do I join Powerbase?
sections[1].faqs[0].answer: You can join Powerbase by purchasing the Gold membership option online or via the Loughborough Sport App. Those who can access a Gold membership are: Unfortunately if you do not qualify through one of these groups, it is not possible to join Powerbase as a Gold member, but you can attend on a pay as you go basis - pay as you go prices (https://www.lboro.ac.uk/sport/memberships-prices/pay-as-you-go-prices/) . You can also join Holywell Fitness Centre by purchasing a Silver membership which is open to everyone in the community. • current Loughborough University students • current Loughborough College students • alumni of Loughborough University • current Loughborough University staff • Key affiliates (https://www.lboro.ac.uk/sport/memberships-prices/discount-categories/) to Loughborough Sport
sections[1].faqs[1].question: Do I have to pay for fitness classes with a gold membership?
sections[1].faqs[1].answer: Complete access to our wide ranging fitness class programme is included with your gold membership. Members can sign up to classes in our studios at both the Sir David Wallace sports hall and Holywell Fitness Centre . You will need to book classes in advance to secure your place on all sessions.
sections[1].faqs[2].question: What are elite training times?
sections[1].faqs[2].answer: Powerbase is a recognised Elite Training Centre, home to many of the country's leading athletes including current and future Olympians and Paralympians. This means you get access to the same world-class gym used by these athletes, however, to facilitate their training, other members cannot access the same side(alternating between Power and Base) from 9:00-12:00 and 14:00-15:30 Monday to Friday and will have the option to only book on the other side (either Power or Base) or alternatively can use Holywell Fitness Centre during these times.
sections[1].faqs[3].question: Is Powerbase two separate gyms and can I use both ?
sections[1].faqs[3].answer: A multi-million pound extension opened in 2023 creates a new combined space of 3,200m 2 , making it one of the world's largest elite strength and conditioning environments. There are now two sides, POWER and BASE. You must book into one side or the other and train within the side you have booked. When entering Powerbase you will find POWER through the left turnstiles and BASE through the far right turnstiles.
sections[1].faqs[4].question: How do I join Holywell?
sections[1].faqs[4].answer: Holywell Fitness Centre is open to everyone! You can join Holywell by purchasing the Silver membership option online or via the Loughborough Sport App. If you are yet to download the app, please do, as all activities, including gym and pool sessions are bookable through the app. You can also attend Holywell on a pay as you go basis.
sections[1].faqs[5].question: Can I access Powerbase gym as a Holywell member?
sections[1].faqs[5].answer: Your Silver membership does not give you access to Powerbase, you would need to upgrade to a Gold membership, however please note that you must be eligible (https://www.lboro.ac.uk/sport/memberships-prices/) to obtain a Gold membership.
sections[1].faqs[6].question: Do I have to pay for fitness classes as a member?
sections[1].faqs[6].answer: Complete access to our wide ranging fitness class programme is included with your Holywell membership. Members can sign up to classes in our studios at both the Holywell Fitness Centre and Sir David Wallace sports hall . You will need to book classes in advance to secure your place on all sessions.

evidence.title: Lboro Sport Faqs
evidence.text:
sections[1].faqs[7].question: Do I have to pay for gym floor classes as a member?
sections[1].faqs[7].answer: Access to our gym floor class programme is included with your Holywell membership. You will need to book classes in advance to secure your place on all sessions.
sections[2].section_title: Overstays
sections[2].faqs[0].question: Do i have to book two 90 minute sessions back to back if i want to extend my workout?
sections[2].faqs[0].answer: No. Remember you have a 15 minute grace period after the end of your 90 minute session to give you time to exit the gym. However, of additional time is required you can now book an overlapping session to extend your session from between 15 to 75 minutes.
sections[2].faqs[1].question: If I've booked onto a coach-led performance session in Powerbase, does this policy apply?
sections[2].faqs[1].answer: Yes. As with all gym sessions, they will last 90 minutes after which you have the same 15 minute grace period to exit the gym. All coaches are aware of this and should not be delaying your exit.
sections[2].faqs[2].question: Do all classes have the same grace period as the gyms?
sections[2].faqs[2].answer: No. As classes cannot be extended in the same way as gym sessions, both gym and floor classes in Powerbase and Holywell and studio classes in Holywell, have a 30 minute grace period after the class is schedule to end.
sections[2].faqs[3].question: How many overstay vouchers do i get?
sections[2].faqs[3].answer: Currently, all active members receive one voucher a month. They're valid for a month, then upon it's expiry, a new voucher will be added to your account as long as you have an active membership. If you've used your voucher, you will receive a new one at this point.
sections[3].section_title: Free Membership access vouchers
sections[3].faqs[0].question: What can I access with my Bronze Vouchers
sections[3].faqs[0].answer: To use the vouchers, make a booking through the Lboro Sport app and select use voucher to pay. Vouchers will expire after 3 months from allocation. Please note that the 1x Powerbase access has now replaced the 1x Class access that was previously included in the Bronze membership for 2023/24. These vouchers will remain valid after August if not used until the 3-month expiry date has passed. • 1x Powerbase access per 3 months (New for 2024/2025) • 1x Holywell access per 3 months
sections[3].faqs[1].question: What can I access with my Silver Vouchers?
sections[3].faqs[1].answer: To use the vouchers, make a booking through the Lboro Sport app and select use voucher to pay. Vouchers will expire after 3 months from allocation. • 4x Powerbase access per year for annual or academic year memberships • 1x Powerbase access per 3 months for monthly paying members
sections[4].section_title: Cancellations
sections[4].faqs[0].question: How do I request a refund?
sections[4].faqs[0].answer: Refunds for memberships cannot be made within facilities. All refund requests need to be placed in writing by the membership holder. This can be done by completing the online cancellation request form (https://www.lboro.ac.uk/sport/memberships-prices/cancellations/) or emailing sportmemberships@lboro.ac.uk (mailto:sportmemberships@lboro.ac.uk) . Please allow up to 7 working days to receive a response, to allow us time to review your request and assess eligibility. Note - Reimbursements will not be refunded to members who are eligible for a discount as an Affiliate to Loughborough Sport after purchasing a membership prior to having their account status updated from community.
sections[4].faqs[1].question: I have bought an academic year or annual membership, can I get a refund?
sections[4].faqs[1].answer: No. If you can no longer use the gym, refunds will only be granted for medical conditions supported by a doctor’s letter or a leave of absence form from the Universit y.
sections[4].faqs[2].question: Who's eligible for a refund?
sections[4].faqs[2].answer: To be eligible for a refund for a membership paid upfront, the below criteria must be met: Those that are eligible to receive a refund, will be informed of the amount they are entitled to receive, after administration and usage fees are deducted. • The membership was purchased within 14 days of the cancellation request being submitted. • You are withdrawing from your studies or employment at Loughborough University - a signed and confirmed leave of absence letter from the University will be required to support the refund request. • You are currently unable to exercise due to medical reasons - a signed doctor's letter will be required to support the refund request, stating your name and a full explanation of why you are not able to train; we cannot except letters that are dated prior to the date your membership was purchased.
sections[4].faqs[3].question: What are administration and usage fees?
sections[4].faqs[3].answer: If the cancellation request has been made within 14 days of the date of purchase and no service has been used in relation to that membership, no additional fees will be applied to the refund. Joining fees and enrollment fees are non-refundable. If a service has been used, members will be charged on a pay as you go basis for each gym, track, pool and / or class use. This will be capped at the monthly fee for that membership (e.g a Silver gym membership of £32 per month or Gold gym membership of £40 per month). This total charge will be subtracted from the price paid. Additionally, if a joining or enrollment fee was paid during membership purchase, this is non-refundable. All refunds granted 14 days after the date of purchase, will incur a £20 administration fee plus a usage fee. For annual / academic year memberships deductions will be calculated through applying the monthly fee for that membership (e.g. Silver membership of £32 per month or Gold membership of £40 per month) to the period of membership used and subtracting from the price paid.
sections[4].faqs[4].question: When will I receive my refund?
sections[4].faqs[4].answer: Please be aware that refunds may take up to 6 - 8 weeks during peak times University admission periods, August - October and January. Online and in person card payments usually take up to 7 working days during non-peak periods and payment will be refunded back to the card that was used to make the initial payment.
sections[4].faqs[5].question: When will my monthly payments end after submitting a cancellation request?
sections[4].faqs[5].answer: Direct debit payments can be cancelled at any time by providing a full calendar month's notice in writing. At every opportunity we will try and cancel your membership as soon as possible. However, due to bank deadlines a payment may still be deducted after we receive your cancellation request. For example, if we receive your cancellation request on the 20 March, a membership payment will still be requested on the 1st or the next working day of April to pay for Aprils membership, meaning your membership won't expire until the 30 April.

evidence.title: Lboro Sport Faqs
evidence.text:
sections[4].faqs[6].answer: If you have a Silver membership you can upgrade to Gold which will allow access to Powerbase gym. Please email sportmemberships@lboro.ac.uk (mailto:sportmemberships@lboro.ac.uk) to request an upgrade. Gold membership includes access to both Holywell fitness centre and Powerbase gym.
sections[5].section_title: Swimming Pool
sections[5].faqs[0].question: Do I need to book to be able to swim in the pool?
sections[5].faqs[0].answer: All sessions must be booked in advanced, either online, via the Loughborough Sport app or over the telephone (01509 226200). From September 1st, 2023 bookings for public swim sessions can be made up to two weeks in advance. Bookings for Performance Programme and AU Club sessions can be made up to 7 days in advance.
sections[5].faqs[1].question: Can I access the building without a booking?
sections[5].faqs[1].answer: Without a valid booking you won't be able to access through the turnstiles to the reception and onto the pool, even if you have a valid membership.
sections[5].faqs[2].question: Are children allowed in public swim times?
sections[5].faqs[2].answer: Children aged 12 years and above are welcome to book a lane swim but must be a competent swimmer and be able to swim continuous lengths.
sections[5].faqs[3].question: Do I have to pay to use the pool as a member?
sections[5].faqs[3].answer: No, if you have purchased either a Gold, Silver or Bronze membership, all levels allow you to access Loughborough University Swimming Pool during public swim sessions at no additional charge. Purple members will benefit by a 10% discount off the pay as you go price.
sections[6].section_title: Car Parking
sections[6].faqs[0].question: Do you have car parking information ?
sections[6].faqs[0].answer: Our parking system is provided by APCOA and uses ANPR (Automatic Number Plate Recognition) technology to charge and enforce parking upon the University's campus. It is important that any vehicle coming onto campus is registered and parks in a designated bay. Students, staff or campus partners: Visitors • Must register on the Loughborough Universities parking portal • Student permits should be approved by the parking team before completing registration • Any Loughborough Sport member paying to use a sport facility through their Loughborough sport / swim school account is permitted up to 2 hours parking free of charge when inputting your car registration details on the tablets located near the reception desk. Tablets are located in the swimming pool, Holywell fitness Centre, Powerbase Gym, Tennis Centre, Hipac, and the Cricket centre. • Please ensure your car is registered with APCOA connect (https://www.apcoaconnect.com/) • Use your APCOA connect account to pay for any charges incurred beyond 2 hours. • If you fail to input your car registration into our facility tablets during every visit Loughborough Sport are not responsible for any charges or parking fines received.
sections[7].section_title: Athletics Centre
sections[7].faqs[0].question: How can I access the Athletics Centre?
sections[7].faqs[0].answer: The Athletics Centre is available during Open sessions with a Gold membership or on a Pay-As-You-Go basis. For further information on access outside of the Open Public Sessions please see click the link below. • If you are a member of the community who is not eligible for a Gold Membership or Loughborough Sport Athletics Partner status, access to Open Public Sessions will be available on a PAYG basis at £5.50 a session with discounts available for Loughborough Sport Purple, Bronze and Silver Members. • If you have a current Gold Membership, either fixed term or pay by monthly direct debit, please note you will need to be in the AU Athletics Club or granted Loughborough Sport Athletics Partner status to access outside of Open Public Sessions.

sections[0].section_title: Frequently asked questions
sections[0].faqs[0].question: When is the deadline to accept my offer and meet any outstanding conditions?
sections[0].faqs[0].answer: If you have made the decision to join us, we encourage you to accept your offer and provide evidence that you meet any outstanding conditions as soon as possible, so that we can ensure the necessary arrangements are in place for you before the start of term and you have enough time to prepare for your studies.
sections[0].faqs[1].question: I can’t get hold of the additional information that you’ve requested in order to consider my application further. What should I do?
sections[0].faqs[1].answer: We understand that there may be delays sourcing the information we need to consider your application (e.g. references, certificates). We are aiming to be as flexible as possible so if you will need extra time to gather requested information, please contact the Doctoral College Office (mailto:pgresearch@lboro.ac.uk) to let us know that there will be a delay.
sections[0].faqs[2].question: What are the English language requirements? What can I do if I haven't fully met these yet?
sections[0].faqs[2].answer: All students are required to meet a minimum standard of English language ability and some departments require a higher minimum level. See our list of English language requirements (https://www.lboro.ac.uk/international/applicants/english/) for more information. There is no need for you to have completed your English language qualifications before you apply – most students are made offers conditional on achieving particular grades in their English language test. If you have not fully met the English language requirements asked for in your offer, it is possible that the school/department may allow you to take one of our English language pre-sessional programmes (https://www.lboro.ac.uk/services/alss/pre-sessional-courses/) . Not all schools/departments will allow students to take an English language pre-sessional programme (https://www.lboro.ac.uk/services/alss/pre-sessional-courses/) , so you should check the guidance carefully (https://www.lboro.ac.uk/international/apply/english-language-requirements/) .
sections[0].faqs[3].question: I've completed my studies but haven't graduated yet
sections[0].faqs[3].answer: We realise that some universities don’t hold their graduation ceremonies until later in the year. We can accept a copy of your final transcript plus a letter from your university to confirm that you have completed your degree and giving your final grade. We call this an award letter and it replaces the degree certificate.
sections[0].faqs[4].question: How will my interview take place?
sections[0].faqs[4].answer: All doctoral research applicants are required to attend an interview as part of the application process. Interviews will take place remotely (by Skype or over the telephone) until further notice.
sections[0].faqs[5].question: Can I visit the University before I start?
sections[0].faqs[5].answer: If you are interested in visiting the Loughborough campus, we offer self-guided tours (https://www.lboro.ac.uk/study/postgraduate/events/find-us/self-guided-tours/) with our own personal itinerary for you to follow. If you are interested in visiting the London campus, please contact london@lboro.ac.uk (mailto:london@lboro.ac.uk) . If you are unable to visit us in person, you can get a feel for life as a doctoral researcher at our Loughborough and London campuses by visiting our location pages (https://www.lboro.ac.uk/study/postgraduate/locations/) and interacting with our 360 degree tours (https://www.lboro.ac.uk/virtualtour/) . You can also watch our Loughborough campus tour video (https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=lUOCxgAp8eg) , and take a look inside our London campus (https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=y25_DKuZGgs) . Please see our events page (http://lboro.ac.uk/study/postgraduate/events/) for up-to-date information on our latest events, including details of web chats (https://www.lboro.ac.uk/study/postgraduate/events/web-chats/) where you can get to know our staff and students and ask any questions you may have.
sections[0].faqs[6].question: Can I defer my start date?
sections[0].faqs[6].answer: Given the current circumstances, we understand that some applicants may be considering deferring their entry. While we are considering deferral requests in the usual manner, we would encourage applicants who had not originally intended to defer their place to take adequate time to fully assess the situation and make an informed decision about their future plans, before choosing to defer. For doctoral researchers who wish to defer, we are able to offer alternative start dates in January, April and July 2021. Applicants can request to defer entry at any point, so there is no rush to make this decision right away.
sections[0].faqs[7].question: Will I need an ATAS Certificate?
sections[0].faqs[7].answer: If you are not a UK national or settled in the UK and plan to undertake postgraduate study in the UK in certain science, engineering or technology subjects, you will need an ATAS certificate before you can apply for a visa or entry clearance. This will be clarified in your offer. Find out more about ATAS certification (https://www.lboro.ac.uk/study/apply/support/atas/) .
sections[0].faqs[8].question: When do research programmes start?
sections[0].faqs[8].answer: There are four available start dates for postgraduate research courses during the academic year: • 1 October • 1 January • 1 April • 1 July
sections[0].faqs[9].question: What funding options are available for research students?
sections[0].faqs[9].answer: Some projects have attached funding, such as a Loughborough University or UK research council studentship (https://www.lboro.ac.uk/study/postgraduate/research-degrees/phd-opportunities/#funding-status=studentship) , but if your doctoral degree does not have attached funding, there’s a range of options available. Our Alumni Bursary (https://www.lboro.ac.uk/study/postgraduate/fees-funding/research-degree-funding/alumni-bursary/) offers a 20% discount on tuition fees to Loughborough alumni who are self-funding their research project. For UK nationals ordinarily resident in England, you could borrow up to £26,445 to cover the cost of your PhD or equivalent research programme with the UK Government PhD Loan. (https://www.lboro.ac.uk/study/postgraduate/fees-funding/research-degree-funding/government-phd-loan/) This can be used to pay for tuition fees or living costs. Other sources of funding are also available through independent organisations and external bodies, charities and trusts. To check whether you are eligible to apply for these or to view your other funding options, please visit our website (https://www.lboro.ac.uk/study/postgraduate/fees-funding/research-degree-funding/) . To supplement your income during your studies, there’s a range of opportunities available. You could become a subwarden in one of our halls of residence or represent the University as a Student Ambassador (https://www.lboro.ac.uk/students/ambassadors/) . Both the University and the Students’ Union list several vacancies, whilst our Careers Network (https://www.lboro.ac.uk/services/careers/) can provide advice on finding and obtaining part-time work. Please note that if you will be studying on a student visa (also known as the Student Route), you must not exceed limits on the number of hours you are permitted to work by UK Visas and Immigration.
